title: Transitions and reduced motion
summary: Animate state changes smoothly and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

scenario.briefing: Buttons snap between states and a spinner animates forever. Add a short transition and disable non-essential motion for users who request reduced motion.

objectives.description: Add a transition to button state changes.
Transfer motion decisions to a new component.

hints: Transition background-color and transform over about 150ms.
Use prefers-reduced-motion to disable non-essential animation.
Add transition: background-color 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease; and @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { transition: none; animation: none; } }.

misconceptions.description: Leaving an infinite animation without a reduced-motion fallback.
misconceptions.testDescription: A reduced-motion media query is present.
misconceptions.feedback: Infinite or large motion must be disabled or reduced when the user requests it.

misconceptions.description: Believing animations are required to understand the interface.
misconceptions.feedback: Motion should enhance, not carry meaning. The interface must work without it.

sections.title: Transitions
sections.body: Transitions interpolate between values over time. Keep them short, around 100-200ms, and animate only transform and opacity when possible.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.body: Some users experience discomfort from motion. The prefers-reduced-motion media query lets you disable or simplify animations while keeping functionality.

vocabulary.definition: A smooth change between CSS values.
A media query matching users who request less motion.
Animation that is not required to use the interface.

hints: Check each statement against motion best practices.
